🇺🇸 Early exit polling in the US midterms shows a bad night could be coming for Trump and the Republicans

Early exit polls on Election Night show President Trump’s approval among voters at just 38%—the lowest midterm rating for a sitting president in nearly two decades, according to NBC, CBS, and CNN. Nearly half of voters say a major reason for their vote is to rebuke Trump, with cost of living, the economy, and frustration with the direction of the country topping the list of concerns.

ABC, CNN, Fox, CBS, and the Associated Press have projected that Democrats Jon Ossoff in Georgia and Mark Warner in Virginia have held their Senate seats. Ossoff’s win was called quickly and by a wide margin in a state Trump carried in 2024; neither is a pickup, so the Senate remains 53-47 for Republicans. Additional safe Democratic holds (including New Hampshire) have also been called. Early returns show Democrats leading in several Republican-held Senate races, including strong early numbers in Kansas, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas, plus solid leads in their must-hold seats such as Michigan.

Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats (and roughly three in the House) to take control of both chambers. Pre-election betting markets gave them roughly a 93–96% chance of flipping the House and about a 74–77% chance in the Senate; those odds have held or edged higher as early results come in. Cook Political Report and other forecasters had projected possible Democratic House gains in the mid-20s.

The Senate fight is still open in the main battlegrounds: Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Ohio, Texas, and others that looked competitive (North Carolina, Nebraska, South Carolina). The final New York Times/Siena polls had Democrats ahead or competitive in most of them. Kalshi and similar markets had priced candidates such as Abdul El-Sayed (Michigan) and Sherrod Brown (Ohio) as clear favorites heading into the night.

Polls have closed across much of the East and Midwest, with early and mail ballots driving strong Democratic numbers so far. Election Day voting is still being counted and could narrow some margins. Alaska’s polls close last, around 1 a.m. Eastern. No chamber has been decided, and close races could take hours or longer. Early signs point to a difficult night for Republicans, but the final picture is still forming.

📡 Iran, Nigeria have ample potential to expand bilateral ties: President Pezeshkian

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for stronger economic, political and cultural cooperation between Tehran and Abuja, saying the two countries have considerable untapped potential to deepen their relations.

President Pezeshkian made the remarks on Tuesday, while receiving the credentials of Hamza Mohammed Salau, Nigeria’s newly appointed ambassador to Iran.
​
Highlighting the positive image of Nigeria and its people among Iranians, the president said the two countries could expand cooperation across a range of fields. He called on the new ambassador to make efforts during his tenure to strengthen bilateral relations, particularly in economic, cultural and political areas.
​
President Pezeshkian also pointed to opportunities for closer cooperation through international organizations and mechanisms, including the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF). He said Iran was ready to draw on all available capacities to develop ties with Nigeria and would welcome any initiative aimed at advancing mutual cooperation.
​
Turning to regional developments, the president said current crises stemmed from the hegemonic and aggressive policies of the United States and the Israeli regime. He urged Muslim countries not to allow the Israeli regime to push the region toward instability and turmoil, stressing the need for regional and Islamic solidarity to promote peace and security.
​
Referring to recent acts of aggression against Iran, President Pezeshkian said the current tensions had been triggered by the other side and that Iran had responded in self-defense. He added that those who believed an attack would force Iran to surrender had miscalculated.
​
He said parties genuinely seeking regional peace and stability should abandon coercion and attempts to impose their will on others, and instead pursue understanding and constructive engagement.
​
For his part, Salau conveyed the warm greetings of Nigeria’s President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to President Pezeshkian and the Iranian people. He also expressed his government’s condolences over the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.
​
The ambassador pledged to work toward stronger bilateral ties, describing economic cooperation, agriculture, and healthcare as promising areas. He also highlighted both countries’ shared positions in some international forums and their cultural affinities, expressing confidence that his tenure would help advance common objectives.

💬 Pezeshkian: Iran welcomes expansion of ties with Cyprus in all fields

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has expressed Tehran’s readiness to expand relations and cooperation with Cyprus across all areas of mutual interest, calling for joint efforts to bring bilateral ties in line with their longstanding historical background and existing potential.

President Pezeshkian made the remarks on Tuesday, during a ceremony to receive the credentials of Antonis Mandritis, the newly appointed ambassador of the Republic of Cyprus to Iran.
​
Noting the long history of relations between the two countries, the Iranian president said their current level of cooperation did not reflect the depth of their historical ties or the opportunities available.
​
President Pezeshkian expressed hope that the new ambassador would play an effective role in strengthening bilateral relations and helping deepen cooperation during his diplomatic mission.
​
Referring to international developments, he said humanity should focus on peaceful coexistence, kindness and constructive engagement rather than war, aggression and the use of force.
​
“Life is short, and it is not worthy of human beings to engage in war, aggression and bullying instead of striving for peaceful coexistence,” the president said, emphasizing the importance of promoting mutual understanding and cooperation to ensure peace and stability for nations.
​
Mandritis, for his part, described his appointment to Iran, which he called a great and historic country, as an honor.
​
Conveying warm greetings from Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides to his Iranian counterpart, the Iranian government, people and Leader of the Islamic Revolution, the ambassador said relations between Iran and Cyprus date back more than 1,000 years.
​
Mandritis pledged to make every effort to strengthen bilateral ties and expand cooperation. He also highlighted Cyprus's commitment to regional and international peace and stability, saying his country would use its position in international forums, including the United Nations, to help reduce tensions and promote dialogue and cooperation among nations.
